hypothesis: The parent's `l_loc` double-counts criticality and its gradient keeps pulling critical pins apart because it is normalised per net (so a huge critical hub net dominates), and it lacks any direct pressure to keep critical pins on the same side; replacing it with a pairwise star-expansion term whose per-pin weight is a *saturating* criticality (crit, not crit^2) times a fan-out damping 1/log(1+k) applied to the *net*, and normalising by the total pin weight, will lower crit_cross without letting hub nets swamp small critical nets, shrinking TNS.
analysis:
(1) Partially. TNS improved on C1/C2 but C3 regressed; crit_cross rose on C1 (0.011→0.016) despite the same-side pressure, so the saturating/damped weighting didn't reliably reduce critical crossings.

(2) C1: cut/wcut down, dWNS +10.5%, dTNS +5.7%, but crit_cross up and repair_flips up (103→121) — more repair churn likely from hub-net damping weakening critical-pin cohesion. C3: crit_cross down (0.069→0.061) yet dWNS −9.8%, suggesting cut reduction didn't translate to timing.

(3) Seed spread is high (std 0.054, min −0.033); not acceptable.

(4) Ablate the 1/log(1+k) damping vs crit-only weighting on C3 to isolate the regression.
